root_cause: ExpenseTracker.over_budget_categories (api.py line 221) filters by s["percent_used"] > 100, but percent_used is computed as round(spent / monthly_limit * 100, 1) in budget_status (utils.py line 126). Python's banker's rounding causes round(100.1, 1) to evaluate to 100.0, so 100.0 > 100 is False and a category spending $100.01 against a $100.00 limit is silently excluded from the over-budget list. Meanwhile budget_status already computes the exact boolean over_budget: remaining < 0 (no rounding), which is True for $100.01 spent. The fix is to filter by s["over_budget"] directly instead of re-deriving from the rounded percent_used.

items.reason: This is the bug site; the wrong predicate (percent_used > 100) loses categories that are genuinely over budget due to rounding.
Computes both percent_used (rounded, lossy) and over_budget (exact, correct); the over_budget field is the authoritative source that over_budget_categories should use.
Correctly assembles and returns the list of status dicts from budget_status; its output already contains the accurate over_budget field.
CLI caller of check_all_budgets and check_budget; already reads status["over_budget"] via _print_budget, so it is unaffected by the fix to over_budget_categories.
